clusters.pick_reason: PR #2493 is the narrower, verifiably end-to-end fix: it updates both participating call sites - session.py's cancel() (removes the erroneous error-response send) and server.py's _handle_request (changes the log/comment from 'duplicate response suppressed' to the correct spec-compliant no-response path) - so client-initiated cancellation is handled consistently across both files. PR #2514 only touches session.py in the shown diff (no corresponding server.py update) and its core mechanism, sending a notifications/cancelled message from within cancel() for timeout/caller-initiated cancellation, is not shown to distinguish that case from a cancellation that originated from the client's own CancelledNotification - the exact case #2493's server.py comment says must get no reply at all. Without that distinction, #2514 risks echoing a redundant notifications/cancelled back to the client that just cancelled the request, i.e. a variant of the duplicate-signaling bug #2493 targets. #2493's smaller, spec-comment-anchored diff is the safer one to keep; any additional timeout/caller-cancellation notification behavior from #2514 should be rebased on top of #2493's fix rather than merged independently.

members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After tokens are loaded from storage (e.g. on process restart), token_expiry_time is never recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired access token as valid and the proactive-refresh path is skipped — forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. clusters.pick_reason: PR #2493 is the narrower, verifiably end-to-end fix: it updates both participating call sites - session.py's cancel() (removes the erroneous error-response send) and server.py's _handle_request (changes the log/comment from 'duplicate response suppressed' to the correct spec-compliant no-response path) - so client-initiated cancellation is handled consistently across both files. PR #2514 only touches session.py in the shown diff (no corresponding server.py update) and its core mechanism, sending a notifications/cancelled message from within cancel() for timeout/caller-initiated cancellation, is not shown to distinguish that case from a cancellation that originated from the client's own CancelledNotification - the exact case #2493's server.py comment says must get no reply at all. Without that distinction, #2514 risks echoing a redundant notifications/cancelled back to the client that just cancelled the request, i.e. a variant of the duplicate-signaling bug #2493 targets. #2493's smaller, spec-comment-anchored diff is the safer one to keep; any additional timeout/caller-cancellation notification behavior from #2514 should be rebased on top of #2493's fix rather than merged independently.
